cells.tense: You are the one still carrying this after everyone else has moved on.
cells.ask: Bring one person into the version of this you actually keep, and let their questions change a piece of it.
cells.core:
You keep a thing alive by using it, and it keeps you. Same table, same practice, same handful of people, and none of it costs you much anymore, because the thing has worked its way into how you move. What you pass along arrives worn and solid, and people lean on it more than they bother to say.

What makes it hold is that you didn't have to force it. It changed shape as the years went and you let it. The ask is to bring one person into the version of this you actually keep — not the tidy telling, the real one, rough edges and all, and let their questions move a piece of it.

cells.tense: You are bracing for the day this finally gives out and no one will hold it.
cells.ask: Name one piece of this you carry alone, and ask one person to carry it with you.
cells.core:
Set down and picked back up, it survives the weeks you don't tend it. You can trust that other people carry their part, and that a quiet stretch is a quiet stretch and not an ending.

You're living ahead of that. Every handover you arrive early, ready to explain, ready to defend, and the watching has grown into more of what you do than the thing itself. Held this long, this kind of persistence starts to look like grip. What you have is real — you just can't feel the floor, because you're holding the whole of it up.

The ask is to name one piece you've been carrying alone and ask somebody to carry it with you. Watch what stays. What doesn't need defending is the part that's finished.
cells.sheetLine: You're defending it hard enough to become the thing in the way.

cells.tense: You stopped carrying it and kept the shape of carrying anyway.
cells.ask: Pick one piece of this you still believe and hand it to one person this week, plainly.
cells.core:
You do the thing because it's yours to do, at the same table, with the same people, and it stays fed. Nothing is being performed.

What's here is quieter. You still show up, still keep the shapes, still do what's familiar, but the thing isn't moving through you the way it once did. When it stopped being answered, the following thinned out, and nobody stood up and said so. You're standing where it used to happen.

The ask is small, and it doesn't need belief first. Pick one piece of this you genuinely still hold and hand it to one person this week. Momentum comes back through a hand, not through effort, and one exchange is enough to find out.

cells.tense: You are holding this open while calling yourself just a regular part of it.
cells.ask: Answer one question about why this matters to you, out loud, once, in your own reasons.
cells.core:
The one who carries a thing like this can point at what they've kept alive and say, that's mine to keep. The following and the open saying of it travel together, and it stays fed without anybody guarding it.

Something is running here that you're not naming. You show up early, you put things back, you call people in, and you talk as though all of it runs on its own. It doesn't. It runs because you keep feeding it, and you haven't told anyone you're the one doing it.

The ask is to answer one question about why this matters to you, out loud, once. Not the group's answer. Yours. What people are drawing on has your hands all over it and you haven't said so yet.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it standing and keep calling yourself a visitor.
